problem: The journal write is awaited inside the plan write after plan.json has already been replaced, so any appendFile failure in recordPlanRevision (src/session/execution-plan-history.ts:68, e.g. EACCES/ENOSPC on plan-history.jsonl) rejects setExecutionPlan/updateExecutionPlan even though the plan was persisted. This contradicts the module's own stated policy in notify() (lines 73-77: 'Persistence already succeeded ... must [not] turn the completed mutation into a rejected promise'), and the same function swallows the cursor failure (history.ts:71) — two opposite failure policies for one secondary side effect.
impact: The caller is told a successful write failed: notify() never runs so the sidebar keeps the old revision, and the agent's retry with the same expectedRevision gets ExecutionPlanConflictError against a plan it did write.

problem: The cursor-update catch only logs to stderr and then returns the entry as if it were committed, with no comment explaining why proceeding is a correct fallback (error-handling.mdc Rule 3). The entry is now in the journal but past the cursor, so readers filter it out.
impact: renderExecutionPlanChangelog (execution-plan.ts:276) silently omits that revision and reports a stale 'latest' revision; the operator catching up sees no record of the change until some later write happens to advance the cursor. Only a stderr line (which in the TUI shell is not where the operator looks) records it.

problem: parseEntry's error names neither the file nor the line, and the JSON.parse SyntaxError above it is not wrapped with the path either — unlike readCursor in the same file, which does exactly this ('Fail with the path so the operator knows which file to remove'). A torn trailing line from the crashed appendFile the cursor is meant to guard against throws here before the cursor filter is applied.
impact: A single bad journal line makes every ExecutionPlanHistory construction and renderExecutionPlanChangelog call fail with 'Invalid entry' or a bare SyntaxError, and the operator has no pointer to plan-history.jsonl.

problem: The ExecutionPlanHistory constructor performs synchronous file I/O (readCursor and readFileSync of the journal) and can throw on a corrupt cursor, violating solid-principles.mdc Iron Law 2 ('A constructor performs no I/O'). It also stores 'readonly dir' which nothing reads.
impact: The class cannot be built from already-loaded entries for tests or reuse, and it forces a blocking sync read into a module (execution-plan.ts) whose other reads are all async.
